newsitem.title: USA: Federal Signal sees strong results in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Federal Signal sees strong results in 1997.

text.p: Federal Signal Corp, which reported record orders, sales, and earnings for 1996, said it expects strong sales and earnings growth in 1997.
"As we enter 1997, we have good reason to anticipate strong sales and earnings growth," said Joseph Ross, chairman, president and chief executive officer, in a statement Monday.

"In 1996, we invested heavily in products and processes; these investments will benefit performance in 1997. At the end of the year our backlogs were at record levels, setting our expectations for strong first half sales," he said.
"Our key markets are strong, and we see no reason this should not continue. Our operational performance continues to improve, signaling expansion in our operating margins," he said.

Federal Signal reported 1996 earnings of $62 million or $1.35 a share, including a $2.8 million after-tax gain on the sale of a small tool business. Net sales increased 10 percent from 1995 to $896.4 million. Orders rose 18 percent in 1996 to $924.6 million while backlogs rose to $280.0 million from $251.4 million a year ago.

All four of the company's groups increased sales and operating income in 1996. Operating income growth was strongest in its Tool and Sign groups, which generally experienced good markets and did not have major new investments in product development in 1996.
For the full year, Vehicle Group sales increased five percent and operating income increased four percent. Orders increased 25 percent.

Excluding results of Bronto, an aerial access manufacturer acquired in August 1995, the group's sales increased three percent and operating income increased six percent. Fire rescue sales increased eight percent while earnings fell eight percent including the sales and earnings of Bronto.

Bronto was unprofitable in the first half of 1996 and this reduced operating margins for the year, Federal Signal said. Bronto improved its results significantly in the second half and achieved a small profit for the year after completing a reorganization of its operations.

In addition to the lower results for Bronto, the group also significantly increased research and development spending to support new product introductions in 1997. Both domestic and foreign orders for fire rescue products increased significantly over the prior year.

Safety Products Group sales increased 22 percent in 1996 and income increased five percent. Orders for the group increased 20 percent. Tool Group earnings increased 11 percent in 1996 on a sales increase of seven percent.
The Sign Group's earnings increased 10 percent on a 16 percent increase in sales.
